validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated pipeline, docket CP22-15-000. Texas Eastern Transmission, LP (Texas Eastern/TETCO, an Enbridge subsidiary) filed an NGA section 7 application on November 10, 2021 (Federal Register notice of application, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2021/12/01/2021-26131/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-application-and-establishing-intervention-deadline, restating the Nov 10 2021 filing date, 1,260,000 Dth/d, $360,306,366 cost). FERC prepared a Final EIS (notice of availability Feb 24 2023, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/02/24/2023-03836/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-availability-of-the-final-environmental-impact-statement-for) describing the same 3.0-mile pipeline segment, New Roads Compressor Station, and modifications at White Castle (Iberville Parish) and Larose (Lafourche Parish) compressor stations, all in Louisiana, feeding the Venture Global Plaquemines LNG terminal via reversed flows on Line 40. Enbridge's own project page (Wayback capture 2024-07-22, https://web.archive.org/web/20240722140816/https://www.enbridge.com/projects-and-infrastructure/projects/venice-extension-project) describes the identical scope in company language: 'Once in-service, the Venice Extension Project will provide 1.26 Bcf/d ... to the Venture Global Plaquemines LNG facility.' The project has since been built and placed in service: FERC authorized partial in-service in an Oct 2024 filing (RP24-1089, 'Venice Extension Partial In-Service...effective 10/12/2024', in https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/10/03/2024-22852/combined-notice-of-filings) and full in-service in a Jan 2025 filing (RP25-348, 'Venice Extension Full In-Service...effective 1/10/2025', in https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-01045/combined-notice-of-filings). EIA's dated Aug2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release (Historical Projects (1996-2024) tab, row 1125, 'Venice Extension Project' / 'Texas Eastern Transmission', Docket CP22-15.) independently shows the same docket moving Applied(2022-01)->Approved(2023-10)->Construction(2024-01)->Part Completed(2024-04/07/10)->Complete(2025-01, completed_date 2024-12-15, year_in_service 2025)->Completed(2026-05/08), never reversed. Natural Gas Intel and East Daley Analytics (trade press, independent of both FERC and EIA) report the same cleared-to-service and first-gas events in 2024-2025 (https://www.naturalgasintel.com/news/plaquemines-lng-pipeline-project-cleared-to-start-service/, https://www.eastdaley.com/media-and-news/plaquemines-lng-takes-first-gas-in-project-milestone, https://www.eastdaley.com/media-and-news/plaquemines-lng-start-lifts-kmi-enbridge-pipes). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- an interstate NGA-certificated transmission expansion of TETCO's Line 40 mainline (Rate Schedule FT-1 firm transportation), not a gathering/process line; EIA lists Pipeline Type=Interstate, Authority=FERC for this same row. DUPLICATE: NOT the same pipe as P0193 (Gator Express Gas Pipeline, Phase I) -- different applicant/owner (Venture Global Gator Express, LLC vs. Texas Eastern Transmission/Enbridge), different FERC docket (CP17-66 vs CP22-15), different physical corridor and different certificated capacity (1,970,000 Dth/d vs 1,260,000 Dth/d). The FERC FEIS explicitly treats them as two interconnecting but separate projects: TETCO's Venice Extension delivers gas to 'an interconnection with a pipeline lateral to be constructed, owned, and operated by Venture Global Gator Express, LLC' -- an interconnection relationship, not identity. Both merely share the same downstream customer (Plaquemines LNG), consistent with the existing P0193 shard's own duplicate finding. LOCATION: Pointe Coupee, Iberville and Lafourche Parishes, Louisiana (both start and end already correctly recorded as Louisiana->Louisiana); no facilities of this specific project are described outside Louisiana. No route geometry is on file for P5519 in the routes repo (geometry: null) so no route-vs-sheet mismatch to adjudicate here.

validity.recommendation: Correct Diameter from 42 to 36 (inches) -- four independent primary/trade sources agree on 36-inch; none support 42.
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded Diameter=42 (in) does NOT match any source found. FOUR independent sources all state the new Venice Extension pipeline segment is 36-inch, not 42-inch: (1) TETCO's original Nov 10 2021 NGA application (Federal Register notice, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2021/12/01/2021-26131/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-application-and-establishing-intervention-deadline): 'a 3.0-mile, 36-inch-diameter pipeline segment ... abandon-in-place a 2.2-mile, 36-inch-diameter existing pipeline segment'; (2) FERC's Final EIS notice of availability, Feb 2023 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/02/24/2023-03836/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-availability-of-the-final-environmental-impact-statement-for): 'an approximately 3.0-mile-long, 36-inch-diameter pipeline segment ... abandonment in place of a 2.2-mile-long, 36-inch-diameter existing pipeline segment'; (3) Enbridge's own project page (Wayback capture 2024-07-22, https://web.archive.org/web/20240722140816/https://www.enbridge.com/projects-and-infrastructure/projects/venice-extension-project): 'Construction of a 3-mile, 36-inch-diameter pipeline segment on Texas Eastern's Line 40'; (4) East Daley Analytics, reporting on the completed, in-service pipeline in Jan 2025 (https://www.eastdaley.com/media-and-news/plaquemines-lng-takes-first-gas-in-project-milestone): 'The 36-inch Venice Lateral runs three miles from TETCO's Line 40 and replaces an existing 2.2-mile segment.' All four documents describe both the OLD (abandoned) 2.2-mile segment AND the NEW 3-mile Venice Extension segment as 36-inch -- there is no design revision on the record where the new segment became 42-inch. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: the existing P0193 (Gator Express) shard's cross_row_leads entry states 'the NEW constructed Venice Extension segment is 42-inch,' attributed to the same East Daley 'takes first gas' article -- that reading appears to be an error (the article's actual sentence, quoted above, says 36-inch for the Venice Lateral). EIA's own dated Aug2026 release (Historical Projects (1996-2024) tab, row 1125, 'Venice Extension Project' / 'Texas Eastern Transmission', Docket CP22-15.) lists Diameter=42 for this docket in every release from 2022 onward, which is likely where GEM's current 42 originated (or a conflation with the adjacent Gator Express project, which IS 42-inch/15-mile/1,970,000 Dth/d per P0193's own sourcing) -- but EIA is one origin and is contradicted here by two FERC filings, the operator's own page, and independent trade press. Recommend Diameter -> 36; Length (3.0 mi) and Capacity (1260 MMcf/d / 1,260,000 Dth/d) are unaffected and confirmed separately in fills[].

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='proposed' is far stale -- LastUpdated 2024-05-29 predates even the partial in-service. Newest dated evidence: FERC's Jan 16 2025 Combined Notice of Filings records TETCO's RP25-348 tariff filing 'Venice Extension Full In-Service' effective Jan 10, 2025 -- i.e. the project (new 3-mile pipeline segment plus New Roads, White Castle and Larose compressor-station work) was fully complete and moving gas by that date. This is corroborated independently by (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which has shown 'Completed'/'Complete' status with completed_date=2024-12-15 and year_in_service_date=2025 since its own 2025-01 release, holding through the newest 2026-08 release with no reversal, and (2) trade press (Natural Gas Intel reporting the FERC clearance to start service, East Daley Analytics' Jan 2025 'takes first gas' reporting describing the built pipeline in past tense). An earlier milestone -- partial in-service -- is separately dated to Oct 12, 2024 by TETCO's own RP24-1089 filing (Sept 26, 2024). Recommending Status='operating'. For StartYear1, the sheet's existing value (2024) matches the partial in-service date (Oct 2024, added StartMonth1=10 here); if GEM's convention for StartYear1 is full/complete commercial operation instead, the value should be 2025/01 -- flagged rather than silently resolved. This directly answers this batch's LNG-feed-pipeline guidance for P5519 (feeds Plaquemines LNG alongside P0193 Gator Express, which the existing P0193 shard already found to be operating since Nov 2024 -- consistent timing, two different interconnecting pipelines both now in service for the same LNG terminal).
